newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia frees activists jailed for subversion.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia frees activists jailed for subversion.

text.p: Indonesia has freed two activists jailed on subversion charges, but one of them vowed on Friday to continue to push for greater openness in the nation's political arena.

Julius Usman, deputy chairman of the unrecognised United Democratic Party of Indonesia (PUDI), told Reuters he and party secretary-general Saleh Abdullah were freed on Thursday night They were arrested on March 5.
However PUDI chairman Sri Bintang Pamungkas, convicted last year for insulting President Suharto, remains in custody in good health and spirits, Usman said.

All three were charged with subversion, which carries a maximum penalty of death, after the PUDI issued greeting cards for the Moslem Eid Al-Fitr celebration calling for a boycott of May 29 elections and for Suharto to be defeated if he stood for re-election in 1998.
"I will not change. I've been doing this for 30 years. This is the point of no return, we need some proper changes in this country," the lawyer and former student activist said.

Usman said it was not clear why Bintang was still held. But it could be because Bintang, who at the time of his arrest was out on bail pending an appeal of his 34-month sentence for insulting Suharto, was refusing to answer questions until the government justified the charges against him.
Usman said he had answered questions, after initially refusing to do so until certain conditions were met. He did not specify those conditions.
Usman said he did not know if the subversion charges against Saleh and himself would be dropped.
The official Antara news agency reported on Friday that 24 students in the Central Java city of Yogyakarta who were detained on Tuesday for advocating a poll boycott had been released.
It said eight others detained for a similar protest on Wednesday in Yogyakarta were still in detention.

An official from the ruling Golkar party, Burhan Magenda, said on Thursday night that those advocating a poll boycott could be charged under a law prohibiting people from inciting others to disobey the government and laws.
Suharto said last month authorities would take action against people who encouraged others not to vote in elections.
Only three parties are allowed to contest the general elections -- Golkar, the Moslem-based United Development Party and the Indonesian Democratic Party.
